param: field altitude / airmass across the session (diagnostic, no pipeline knob)

observation.instrument: Siril 1.4.4 register -2pass regdata via inspect_stage.py, pooled per set (qa_work/frame_metrics.json); plate scale 18.0031 arcsec/px from the astrometry.net mount-probe solve
observation.shape: STEPS between sets, not a smooth within-set drift: within-set FWHM change is -0.7 / +2.7 / +2.3 / -0.3 pct

hypothesis: The field descends through the session, so rising airmass plus differential refraction degrades FWHM and elongates stars (which would also make this dataset the hour-angle discriminator BACKLOG:one-sided-band asks for).
test: Hour-angle change needs no site: dH = sidereal(t - t0) - (RA_center - RA_center_0) from the four mount-probe solves. Altitude then bounded over the whole plausible site range for the rig's UTC-4 stamps (lat 25-47 N, lon 67-85 W).

result.altitude_trend: RISING at every one of the 15 sampled lat/lon combinations
result.airmass_direction: FELL through the session in every case

verdict: NULL — REFUTED. Airmass fell while FWHM rose, so rising airmass and differential refraction cannot be the cause. Seeing should have improved.

also_refuted.dew: the recorded dew signature pairs rising FWHM with a 13-16 pct nstars CRASH; first-block nstars here are flat-to-rising (1286/1275/1256/1308)
also_refuted.field_content_as_a_confound: the within-set nstars decline is galactic latitude (b +0.75 -> -3.73 across set-01); set-02's re-aim to b +1.78 recovers the count to 1275, which no progressive optical fault can do

still_open: The +9.9 pct FWHM / -6.1 pct roundness session trend is UNATTRIBUTED. Remaining candidates: focus shift with cooling optics, seeing independent of airmass, and handling at the re-aims. A directional term is implied because roundness falls while the in-exposure trail is fixed (2.5 s at Dec +41.5 to +43.2 gives a constant ~1.56 px) and pure defocus is symmetric.
named_test: The FWHM step size orders with the inter-set gap (51 s -> -0.7 pct, 3 m 52 s -> +3.7 pct, 9 m 39 s -> +6.7 pct), n=3. A handling disturbance settles, so it predicts the frames just after a re-aim are the WORST of their set; measured, sets 02 and 03 are the opposite (FWHM RISES monotonically within them). That disfavours handling and leaves a continuous mechanism, untested.
scope: ONE session, four sets, one rig. Diagnostic only: reads headers and solves, no deliverable pixel, no pipeline knob.

instrument: scripts/qa/coverage_probe.sh (Siril: register -2pass real members -> constant-fill twins -> seqapplyreg stored transforms -> stack sum); full-depth mask analysed off the map
probe_caveat: the probe's value/1000 contract did NOT hold on this run — the sum SATURATED at 1.0, so coverage was read as a*17/max instead. The map's quantisation is clean (levels land on 11..17), which is what makes the ratio read safe. Anyone reproducing this must check the raw max before dividing by 1000.
verdict: min RETAINED. It captures 88% of the best available full-depth rectangle — not the pathological case the registry records (min kept 36% of the true common area on 50 mutually rotated members). The available upside is +14% area (12.20 vs 10.73 Mpx, +6.8% linear).
why_not_max: Taking the +14% needs a max compose plus a coverage-thresholded crop, and that crop carries the measured numpy-vs-Siril y-origin trap that once shipped a zero-coverage wedge into a render. The area gain does not justify introducing a verified-crop step on a product that is already uniform-depth by construction.
reference_pinned: sessions/july31/work/groups_set-02/sub_03.fit (member 8) — central in pointing (Dec 42.79 against a 41.50-43.17 span) and in time. Pinning matters because register -2pass's auto reference sets the canvas orientation and, via -norm=addscale, the composite's raw channel balance.
weighting: --weight=nbstack — members are not equal depth (15 x 100 frames + 2 x 130)

status: CLOSED — band REPRODUCED and characterised; the named discriminator does NOT resolve on one night
instrument: scripts/qa/star_stations.py (Siril crop + findstar, open gate) at fixed equal-area stations, radius 350, offsets 700/1300, drift axis derived EXTERNALLY from each product's own solved WCS (+RA direction at the field centre) — never fitted from the detections

combine.note: canvas 4083x2627 is smaller than a per-set canvas, so the perpendicular +-1300 station falls outside; offsets reduced to 700/900 for the combine only

AXIS_SIGN_TRAP: set-04's WCS-derived drift axis is 0.96 deg where sets 01-03 read 165.8/168.6/176.8. That is a mod-180 wrap, so set-04's 'along+' station is the PHYSICALLY OPPOSITE side from the other three. Comparing the raw 'along+1300' column across sets compares opposite sides of the frame and inverts set-04's result. Always read the axis angle with the station table.
results: The one-sided along-drift band REPRODUCES on july31 — same signature and same physical side as the july27 record, on a different night and a different route (groups, not single-pass).

NO CENTRE BAND: the centre station is the BEST or near-best in every set (2.50-2.68 px) and in the combine (2.59). The paraxial-error band a community lensfun profile writes (july14: centre 5.30 vs perpendicular 3.60) is ABSENT — the FITTED model is doing its job.
The excess over centre grows monotonically across the session: 9.0 -> 15.6 -> 18.1 -> 19.2 pct.
discriminator_verdict: INCONCLUSIVE, and the reason is structural. Within ONE night hour angle, elapsed time and altitude are collinear (H = H0 + sidereal*t, minus small re-aims), so the growth cannot be attributed to hour angle rather than to time or to whatever drove the session-wide FWHM trend. BACKLOG:one-sided-band's named discriminator needs sets at MATCHED time and DIFFERENT hour angle, which one night cannot supply.
refraction_disfavoured_not_eliminated: The field ROSE through the session (altitude increasing at every plausible site — see fwhm_session_trend_airmass_hypothesis). Simple differential refraction scales with tan(zenith distance), so it predicts the band SHRINKING as the field rises; the band GREW. That disfavours plain refraction. It does not eliminate a full refraction model, because the elongation projects onto the drift axis through the parallactic angle, which also changes.
against_a_pure_drift_length_residual: set-04 has the SHORTEST drift (473 px vs 1151/912/906) yet the LARGEST excess over centre (19.2 pct), so band magnitude does not track drift length either. set-04 is also shaped differently: its centre is the session's best (2.50) while BOTH along stations degrade (2.98/2.78), rather than one side only.
scope: ONE night, four sets, one rig, one lens/focal, groups route. Station medians of Siril's own per-star fits; n=918-1224 per station.

hypothesis: PRE-REGISTERED (prompt step 4): find what differs between july31's broken fit and aug06's clean ones — frame content, moon gradient, or subset window
verdict: UNTRUSTWORTHY FIT — july31 stays under the pinned incumbent. The patched procedure (gauss 3, satellite-free mid-burst window DSC_3893..4036 step 13) removes the old starvation (217 raw CPs vs the ledger's 66) but converges to a sign-alternating order-of-magnitude curve (a=-0.0311 b=+0.0986 c=-0.0660 after strict prune, 104 CPs, checkpto 0.02/0.06) that contradicts product-level evidence: july31's products under the PINNED model are the family floor (off-axis 0.16-0.47 px), impossible if the true state were this curve.
mechanism: MEASURED, CP spatial coverage (min-half-dim r over both endpoints of every strict-prune CP): july31 bins (0/.25/.5/.75/1.0/1.25+) = [0,45,5,143,15,0], x span 540-5254, y 465-3919 — a 5-CP hole across r 0.5-0.75 and ZERO corner support; aug06 s02/s03 same procedure = [3,46,65,45,54,36] and [2,104,84,41,56,13], full spans. A radial polynomial over two narrow bands with a hole oscillates through the unconstrained field. Banding is night-level (98%-moonlit sky gradient compresses usable star contrast into a sensor region; all four july31 flats carry the moon signature), so another window faces the same coverage.

hypothesis: PRE-REGISTERED (BACKLOG:aircraft-rejection-retest, written before this session): the ratified KEEP of july31/set-03's aircraft crossing (DSC_5151..5158, 8 of 500) rests on per-pixel sigma rejection removing a minority. Nil on-track residual between the ratified stack and an aircraft-excluded control = the keep is free depth; a visible trail or level step = the keep was wrong and becomes a recorded cull.
route: groups (the STANDING route) — ratified 500 frames -> 5 groups of 100; control 492 frames -> 5 groups (2x99 + 3x98). Both arms: same master dark, same skyflat_set-03, GESD `rej g 0.3 0.05` per group (98/99/100 all sit in the >50 GESD band), -framing=min, 5-member plain-mean compose with no rejection. The 8 frames are the only knob.
verdict: REJECTION CONFIRMED — the ratified keep is verified free depth at this route. Siril's own rejection maps show the aircraft's trails as the ONLY extra rejections the 8 frames cause, and the stack residual measured ON that track is nil.
instrument: Siril throughout: `stack ... rej g 0.3 0.05 -rejmaps` (the per-pixel record of which samples GESD discarded), `isub`, `boxselect`+`stat`. In-house code only located the track (block-averaging the rejection-map difference) so the Siril measurement could be aimed at it.

measured.trail_amplitude_per_frame: Siril stat, 40x40 boxes stepped along the audit's own geometry: DSC_5155 on-trail mean 1229.3 ADU / sigma 293.4 / max 3195 against the SAME box on aircraft-free DSC_5100 at 1138.0 / 23.0 / 1566; the along-track neighbour 1215.7 / 251.1 / 2786; boxes at +-0.4L and every y-flipped box read the clean frame's level, so the geometry AND the coordinate convention are verified by the data, not assumed. Sky ~1140 ADU, per-frame bgnoise ~12 ADU: trail pixels are a 60-170 sigma per-pixel outlier.
measured.coverage_per_pixel: audit centroids move ~820 px/frame (full scale) against a ~740 px trail length, so the trail crosses each sky pixel in ~1 frame. At groups@100 that is 1/100 = 1% against GESD's 0.30 outlier-fraction cap.
measured.rejection_map_group4: high-rejection 1.276/1.403/1.302% per channel; map median 1310.5 = 2.00 frames, max 19660.5 = 30.00 frames = exactly the 0.30 cap.
measured.rejection_map_difference: WITH minus WITHOUT (100- vs 92-frame stacks of the same group, same chain) contains ONLY the aircraft's twin-trail segments, stepping across the canvas in 8 consecutive positions; everything else is at the map difference's own noise. Median -114.0 ADU = exactly the predicted (2/92 - 2/100) x 65535 = -114.0 scale step between the two denominators, which independently calibrates the map. The track's amplitude is +1 frame (655.35 ADU), matching the ~1-frame-per-pixel coverage.
measured.on_track_residual: stack difference (100-frame minus 92-frame, same canvas), 60x60 boxes at six points on the track the rejection map identified: 4.30 4.40 4.30 4.50 4.40 4.20, mean 4.35 ADU. Perpendicular controls at +-200 and +-400 px: 4.40 / 4.42 / 4.37 / 4.48. Whole-frame 4.50 (the two stacks' own -output_norm anchors). On-track minus off-track = -0.07 +- 0.08 ADU.
measured.sensitivity: an entirely UNREJECTED trail would raise a 60x60 on-track box by ~0.9 ADU (766 ADU/frame per trail pixel / 100-frame group mean, 11.6% box fill). Measured 0.00 +- 0.08, so rejection removed >= 91% and the result is consistent with 100%.

the_specified_test_is_under_powered: The BACKLOG item's own closing test — difference the two FULL-SET products — was executed and is flat (88 boxes of 400 px on the common canvas, box means 33.1-33.3 ADU, strongest/median 1.01; the whole difference is a uniform pedestal from the two builds' independent -output_norm anchors). But it cannot settle the question either way: after the /100 group mean and the /5 plain-mean compose, even a totally unrejected trail contributes only ~1.5-4.1 ADU per trail pixel, which spread over a 400 px box is 0.02-0.06 ADU against a measured 0.2 ADU box-to-box spread. The discriminating measurement is at the GROUP, where rejection actually happens.
declared_deviation: the rejection-map and on-track-residual probes ran WITHOUT the darktable warp. The warp is a geometric resample and cannot change whether a 60-170 sigma sample is an outlier among 100; everything bearing on rejection (same 100 frames, same masters, same calibrate command, same rejection clause, same registration model) is what the chain runs. The full-set A/B, which DID include the warp, is consistent.
records: rejection maps + difference + on-track stats under ~/.cache/astro-imaging/b3_rejmap{,_without} and b3_rejdiff (scratch, regenerable); control stack web/results/july31/stack_set-03ctl_full.fit deleted after this verdict per the item's own instruction.

status: CLOSED — NULL with controls. The flat attribution is FALSIFIED as the dominant term and the measurement is a registered DEAD END; the untracked 3.11%/241 sigma figure is retired as UNVERIFIED.
param: diagnostic — no pipeline knob; nothing gated, nothing rewritten
instrument: scripts/qa/object_tilt.py — Siril findstar (roundness floor 0.05, layer 1) for detection, position and RA/Dec through each sub-stack's own astrometry.net solve; Siril psf for every flux as APERTURE photometry at a forced radius against setphot's local annulus (r = 10 and 16 px, annulus 20-30 px); in-house: sky cross-match (34" unique-within-3x) + weighted LS of m_ij = M_i + z_j + ax*u_ij + ay*v_ij over the 52 already-solved groups sub-stacks
pre_registration: datasets/aug09/tilt_corpus_prediction.json, committed at 17b2ee7 BEFORE 10 of the 12 sets were measured
no_clip_control: Siril psf reports a failed measurement as m=<value>+/-9.9990; every measurement at or above that sentinel is rejected, never averaged. A 30 px boxselect fails and a 40-160 px box is stable to 1e-4 mag, so the box is pinned at 60.

measured.positive_control_planted_ramp: Siril imul of a linear card, edge ratio 1.222184: the instrument moved +9.85 points where +7.94 was expected — recovery 1.24x overall, 0.95x on the best-levered block pair (rotation 2.37 deg). Per-pair recovery runs 0.14x-5.2x and tracks the pair's lever.
measured.identity_control_uniform_card: the same path with k=0 (card exactly 1.0) moved the full fit and ALL SIX block pairs by exactly 0.00 points — the card path is inert.
measured.internal_falsification_block_pairs: one sensor-fixed field must give one answer from every block pair; the median within-set spread across the corpus is 529 percentage points (aug09/set-01: +56.9, -19.5, -64.8, -80.3, -88.0, -92.5%).
measured.geometric_blocker: a linear sensor-fixed mode is EXACTLY absorbed by the per-star and per-block nuisances under a pure translation, so the 503-1220 px drift is not the lever. Field rotation is: 0.69-3.76 deg per set, giving an effective lever of 9.2-34.3 px (median 29.1) on a 5769 px frame — 0.5%, a ~200x extrapolation. --selftest 4a: a planted +0.100 mag returns -0.046 +- 0.0001 with the lever at 0.00 px, so a degenerate fit reads confidently WRONG, not unidentified.
measured.time_varying_sensor_fixed_gradient: freeing a per-block gradient measures a within-set drift of 0.0398-0.4245 mag across the frame (median 0.1486), MONOTONE in block order in 10 of 12 sets. Its leak into a shared-gradient fit (delta/theta) is 0.74-13.45 mag and exceeds the measured shared gradient in every set.
measured.corpus_prediction: P1 sign 8/12 FAIL; P2 built-in null aug06/set-03 predicted +2.6% measured +223 +- 28% FAIL; P3 extremes opposite sign PASS; P4 Spearman rho +0.678 p 0.015 (below the pre-registered 0.7) FAIL; P5 |measured| <= |flat dose| 0/12 FAIL — every set exceeds its own flat's dose by 1.4x-86x, median 8.1x.
measured.corpus_range: measured tilt -77% .. +1605% against a predicted -35.8% .. +47.7%; per-night means july31 +113%, aug06 +82%, aug09 +578%.
measured.n_and_depth: 2545-3823 stars per set, 4-5 blocks (july31/set-04 has 2), faintest admitted fitted amplitude 0.00500 in every set, residual rms 0.0175-0.0336 mag, chi2/dof 10-30.
measured.tool_search: Siril seqpsf -wcs= converts the sky coordinate to pixels ONCE and measures that same area in every image (m -2.104 vs +3.55/+5.05/+3.63 on one real star across four blocks; -followstar does not repair it). light_curve is a time series against comparison stars. SCAMP is not packaged (no apt candidate). source-extractor 2.28.2 IS installed and works (47,971 objects in 3.1 s, FLUX_APER at two radii, BACKPHOTO_TYPE LOCAL) but is another per-image photometer, not a cross-image solution.
measured.null_control_interleaved_halves: interleaved halves of aug09/set-01 (249 even frames against 249 odd, both through the same undistort chain and solved the same way): the two products span the same drift, so every star's flux is the average of the SAME sensor positions in both and THE PREDICTED TILT IS EXACTLY ZERO. MEASURED +49.08 +- 4.97% at r=10 px and +50.82 +- 5.65% at r=16 px, 3086 stars, residual 0.0085 mag, chi2/dof 3.74, lever 27.9 px — i.e. an 11.8-sigma reading of a quantity that is zero by construction. THE FLOOR IS 49 PERCENTAGE POINTS, and the formal sigma is meaningless, which is the same lesson --selftest 4a teaches on synthetic data. Note the halves are NOT co-registered: Siril picked a different reference frame for each, leaving -2.37 deg and 103 px between their canvases — which is why the lever did not collapse and the null is a fair test of the live configuration rather than a degenerate one.
measured.discrimination_ratio: the planted-ramp control's discrimination AGAINST THE FLOOR is 0.20x — the Siril imul ramp (edge ratio 1.222184) moves the answer +9.85 points against a measured floor of 49.08, i.e. the planted signal is five times SMALLER than what the instrument reports when the truth is zero. The iterative-flat NULL met 48-62x on this standard. Against the INERT arm the discrimination is total: the uniform card moves every number, and every block pair, by exactly 0.00. Re-running the controls reproduced -54.40% / +9.85 points / recovery 1.2408 to every digit.

verdict: NULL — and the null is the deliverable. The interleaved-halves control reports +49.1 +- 5.0% where the truth is zero, so the FLOOR IS 49 PERCENTAGE POINTS. The instrument itself is sound (planted ramp recovered at 1.24x, uniform card inert); the DATA'S GEOMETRY is what fails: the linear mode is degenerate under translational drift, and for a FIXED camera the atmosphere is sensor-fixed and airmass-shaped exactly like the flat's baked-in sky term, so no sensor-frame star-photometry fit can apportion them. Both blockers are independent and either is fatal.
refutes: that the sky x V object tilt can be sized catalogue-free from the drift (BACKLOG:calibration-evidence's 'test that needs no catalogue'); and that the repo's long-quoted 3.11% / 241 sigma is a verified magnitude — it has no tracked record and is not reproduced.
scope: 12 real light sets, 3 nights, one body/lens/focal, 52 solved sub-stacks. The MECHANISM of the defect (a horizon-fixed gradient cannot drift out of a median of un-registered lights; dividing by a flat that absorbed it tilts the object) is untouched — only its magnitude is unmeasured.
